features.ip_note: Premium residential+mobile pool $10/GB PAYG, $9 Starter, $8 Base, $7 Advanced (5/15/50 GB shared traffic included on paid plans); shared pool otherwise; BYO HTTP/SOCKS5/SSH/WireGuard etc. on all plans.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv 4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Quoted up-to 90/390/990 hours do not precisely equal fee divided by rate (29/.30=96.67 etc.). Use explicit fee and dollar rates; do not invent a second included-hours allowance.
Fingerprint cpu/ram/OS/GPU values are browser identity fields, not server hardware or actual Windows/macOS guests.
CAPTCHA is included on pricing page, but docs overview mentions usage-billed solving. Record conflict rather than silently guaranteeing unlimited solves. Shared and premium proxies are distinct.

Browser-session regimes carry os ["linux"] (engine convention: a hosted browser serves a Linux-side workload). Surfsky does not publish the host OS; fingerprint OS values are spoofed identity fields. Rates re-checked 2026-09-28 on surfsky.io/pricing: $0.35/$0.30/$0.25/$0.20 per browser-hour on PAYG/Starter/Base/Advanced, reserved fleet from $0.03/h.
Region is account-wide (Germany or US); it can be changed at most once every 24 h with no browsers running, and on some plans it is assigned by support (region_managed).

fleet.tiers: PAYG 10; Starter 15; Base 50; Advanced 199; Custom negotiated.
fleet.notes: 10 fits PAYG; 50 Base; 300/1,000 need custom reserved fleet. Browser sessions only. Profile API calls (including browser starts) are rate-limited per minute and per hour (docs example 60/min, 1,000/h; per-account values in X-Ratelimit headers), so many simultaneous starts can hit the request limit before the slot limit.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: For persistent profiles, a normal stop saves the selected browser state.
snapshot_auto.note: Hosted antidetect browser, not a VM. Persistent profiles save selected storage (cookies, passwords, bookmarks, optionally localStorage, extension state, history, service workers) on a normal stop and restore it on next start: profile persistence, not a machine/memory snapshot (open tabs and page memory are not kept). Whether an inactivity-timeout stop also saves is not stated; 'Recent unsaved state may be lost' on failures.

harness_api.quote: Use the REST API to start and stop browsers, manage saved profiles, and configure proxies and extensions. A start request returns the WebSocket URL used by your automation framework.
harness_api.note: Product is a hosted antidetect browser controlled via CDP/Playwright/Puppeteer/ChromeDriver or Surfsky's own SDK, plus REST endpoints for profiles/proxies/scrape. Searched the full llms-full.txt dump for 'agent', 'harness', 'mcp', 'langchain', 'llm' — zero matches. No agent/LLM-harness API or MCP server exists. Confirms existing 'no' with direct evidence.

egress_allowlist.quote: Block domains with `proxy_blacklist` in the start request:
egress_allowlist.note: Per-session domain deny-list with wildcards, enforced at the network layer outside the page ('Requests to blocked domains do not reach the proxy or consume metered proxy traffic.'). Deny-list only, no allow-only/default-deny mode; IP/CIDR entries are NOT blocked (they bypass the tunnel); ignored on OpenVPN sessions. Plus domain_routes to send domains via other proxies, and a full-tunnel kill switch (firewall blocks traffic outside the proxy/VPN tunnel).

guest_firewall.note: No shell/root access: you get a browser over CDP in a provider-managed container. Surfsky itself runs a firewall/kill switch in the browser's network namespace ('A firewall blocks traffic outside the tunnel, including DNS lookups.' - intro-to-surfsky).

secret_proxy.quote: Export a stopped saved profile's cookies as JSON or Netscape text. Cookies must be enabled in its storage settings. The response contains data.cookies.
secret_proxy.note: Login persistence is via profile cookie/storage export-import, not a secret-injection proxy. Docs explicitly tell callers to keep their own API tokens and any typed secrets out of logs ('Keep tokens in server-side environment variables or your secret store... Avoid logging typed secrets.') — the caller manages credentials themselves; Surfsky provides no vault/credential-injection feature for site logins. Confirms existing 'no' with direct evidence.

volume_attach.quote: A one-time session starts without a saved profile. Its profile state is discarded when it stops. A persistent profile saves the storage types you enable and can be started again.
volume_attach.note: Full API surface (sessions, persistent profiles, cookies export/import, extensions upload, scrape) has no volume/disk/filesystem-attach concept anywhere in the docs; the only durable state is browser-profile storage (cookies, localStorage, etc.), not a mountable/attachable disk. Confirms existing 'no' with direct evidence.

isolation.quote: Surfsky connects your proxy or VPN, or a proxy from a Surfsky pool, inside the container's network namespace.
isolation.note: Surfsky is a hosted-browser service, not a VM/sandbox provider; each browser session runs in a container-scoped network namespace.

image_oci.quote: Start a browser with an API request, connect Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or a Surfsky SDK to it, and stop it when the run is done. Surfsky hosts the browsers and the proxies.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a managed Chromium browser, not a general-purpose machine that boots from a container image)

docker_inside.quote: Start a browser with an API request, connect Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or a Surfsky SDK to it, and stop it when the run is done. Surfsky hosts the browsers and the proxies.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no shell/root access to run Docker; you get a browser reachable over CDP/WebDriver.

nested_virt.quote: Start a browser with an API request, connect Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or a Surfsky SDK to it, and stop it when the run is done. Surfsky hosts the browsers and the proxies.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, no /dev/kvm or general compute access is exposed.

desktop.quote: Screencast streams a page's screen over WebSocket. It is view-only. Use DevTools when you need to inspect elements or interact with the browser.
desktop.note: Only the single browser tab is streamed view-only (JPEG frames) for observing runs; there is no VNC/RDP graphical desktop of a full machine.

ssh.quote: You can also supply an HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5, SSH, Shadowsocks, OpenVPN, or WireGuard connection.
ssh.note: not offered: 'SSH' here is a supported upstream proxy protocol for outbound traffic, not SSH access into the Surfsky machine itself; there is no shell access to the browser host.

snapshot.quote: For persistent profiles, a normal stop saves the selected browser state.
snapshot.note: A persistent profile saves selected browser storage (cookies, passwords, bookmarks, optionally localStorage/extensions/history/service workers) on stop and restores it on next start; this is profile-storage persistence, not a running-process memory snapshot, so treated like a filesystem-level snapshot rather than 'mem'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: For persistent profiles, a normal stop saves the selected browser state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Profile state is saved automatically on a normal stop; there is no API/CLI call to take a snapshot/checkpoint at an arbitrary point while the browser keeps running.

fork.quote: A persistent profile runs one browser at a time. Starting it again returns the running session and ignores the settings sent with that request... Use a separate profile for work that runs in parallel.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no clone-a-machine operation; parallel work requires creating a separate profile from scratch, not forking an existing one.

fork_running.quote: A persistent profile runs one browser at a time.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no fork concept at all, so cloning a running machine is not possible).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: For persistent profiles, a normal stop saves the selected browser state.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Saved state is profile storage (cookies/passwords/etc.), not a memory image, and there is no fork operation at all.

pause_resume.quote: Explicit stop. For persistent profiles, a normal stop saves the selected browser state. Wait for completion before starting the next run.
pause_resume.note: Only stop (which discards the running browser and its concurrency slot, saving profile storage) and start (which spins up a fresh browser process) are offered; there is no pause that keeps a suspended process resident at reduced billing.

wake_on_request.quote: Creation does not start a browser. Each start restores saved profile state.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A stopped profile requires an explicit POST /profiles/{uuid}/start call; there is no mechanism where an incoming request to a URL automatically wakes a stopped browser.

persistent_disk.quote: storage_options selects the data saved with the profile: Website cookies, Browser-saved passwords, Bookmarks, Local storage...
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. What persists is selected browser profile storage, not a general filesystem/disk you can write arbitrary files to.

volume_shared.quote: A persistent profile runs one browser at a time.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; there is no volumes/filesystem concept at all (per feature_evidence.volume_attach in the card), so a volume shared across running machines does not exist.

live_resize.quote: PAYG / Starter / Base / Advanced browser-hour plans priced per hour with fixed concurrency tiers.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CPU/RAM is exposed to resize; plans/tiers only change price-per-hour and concurrency limits, chosen at start time, not live-resized mid-session.

agent_harnesses.quote: Headless cloud browsers with real device fingerprints; CDP connection from Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium; REST request-response mode without a browser session.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Surfsky offers a browser reachable via CDP/WebDriver/REST for you to drive with your own code or agent; it does not preinstall/offer coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) as templates.

own_agent_api.quote: Agent Browser — Give your AI agents reliable web access at scale. CDP connection from Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. 'Agent Browser' is marketing of the same CDP/API browser product for use by external AI agents; Surfsky does not run its own browsing/computer-use/research agent that you call via API.

mcp_server.quote: Use the Python and TypeScript SDKs to manage browser sessions and automate web pages.
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is mentioned anywhere in the docs (llms-full.txt); only REST API + Python/TypeScript SDKs are offered to control sessions.

lang_python.quote: The Python (/sdk/python#process-items-concurrently) and TypeScript (/sdk/typescript#process-items-concurrently) SDKs provide map() and browser pools with a concurrency setting and managed cleanup.
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for driving the browser/API.

lang_node.quote: The Python (/sdk/python#process-items-concurrently) and TypeScript (/sdk/typescript#process-items-concurrently) SDKs provide map() and browser pools with a concurrency setting and managed cleanup.
lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/JavaScript (Node.js) SDK for driving the browser/API.

public_ipv4.quote: Start a browser with an API request, connect Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or a Surfsky SDK to it, and stop it when the run is done.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no machine with an assignable public IPv4; the browser is reached via a Surfsky-issued CDP/WebSocket/API URL, and outbound traffic uses proxy exit IPs, not an IP owned by the customer machine.

inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The only HTTPS/WSS endpoints are Surfsky's own gateway paths (CDP/DevTools/ChromeDriver/screencast) into the browser protocol; there is no way to expose an arbitrary port/service running inside the machine via an HTTPS URL.

ingress_rules.quote: Calling a host that does not serve your account returns 403 namespace_not_allowed.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access control is account/token-based for Surfsky's own API/CDP gateway; there is no concept of provider-side ingress rules (allowlists/security groups) for ports on a customer machine, since no customer-exposed ports exist.

egress_http_rules.quote: Block domains with proxy_blacklist in the start request... IP/CIDR entries are NOT blocked (they bypass the tunnel); ignored on OpenVPN sessions.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is domain-level only (proxy_blacklist deny-list plus domain_routes), not HTTP method/path-level rules.

static_egress_ip.quote: When you save a pool selection, the profile stores one proxy from that pool and reuses it on every run. The exit IP behind a residential or mobile proxy still changes between sessions; use session control when the IP must stay the same.
static_egress_ip.note: Sticky/session-scoped IP is available for the duration of a session (session_minutes / keep_ip) but the exit IP is a pooled residential/mobile proxy IP, not a fixed IP dedicated to the account across sessions.

gpu.quote: PAYG / Starter / Base / Advanced browser-hour plans; Reserved dedicated fleet from-rate.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Surfsky sells hosted browser sessions billed per browser-hour, not GPU compute; fingerprint 'renderer'/GPU fields only spoof a browser's reported GPU identity.

windows.quote: A one-time profile can omit fingerprint entirely; the default OS is Windows.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. 'Windows' here is a spoofed browser fingerprint OS value, not an actual Windows machine/VM; the host runs a Linux-side Chromium engine per the card's os convention.

macos.quote: A fingerprint is the set of browser and device properties a website can observe... GPU and WebGL parameters, OS-specific screens and fonts...
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. macOS only appears as a possible spoofed fingerprint identity, not an actual macOS guest machine.

arm64.quote: os_arch: Architecture, such as x86 or arm
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. 'arm' is a spoofed fingerprint field for the emulated device identity, not the actual CPU architecture of the underlying host machine (host arch is not published).

self_host.quote: Surfsky hosts the browsers and the proxies.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Surfsky is a fully hosted SaaS; no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option is documented.

byoc.quote: Surfsky hosts the browsers and the proxies.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No bring-your-own-cloud deployment is documented; Surfsky runs the infrastructure itself in its own two regions (Germany, US).

open_source.quote: Cloud antidetect browser that runs browsers in the cloud and passes the web's toughest anti-bot challenges over API and CDP.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The core hosted-browser/anti-detect product is closed-source; only client SDKs are public, not the core service.

sso.quote: The shell examples use SURFSKY_API_BASE_URL and SURFSKY_API_TOKEN; set them as shown in credentials.
sso.note: Authentication is a single API token per account (X-Cloud-Api-Token); no SAML/OIDC SSO login is documented for the dashboard.

eu_data_residency.quote: Surfsky runs in two regions, Germany and the United States. Choose the one closest to your automation worker in the dashboard.
eu_data_residency.note: An account's whole browser workload can be run in the Germany (EU) region.

max_session_h.quote: The browser stops after browser_settings.inactive_kill_timeout seconds without a CDP command, ChromeDriver request, or scrape. The default is 30 seconds; an open but idle connection does not count.
max_session_h.note: No documented hard maximum session duration was found; a session ends only via explicit stop or a configurable inactivity timeout (default 30s, raisable), so an actively-used session can in principle run indefinitely.

soc2.quote: PAYG / Starter / Base / Advanced browser-hour plans; Reserved dedicated fleet from-rate.
soc2.note: No trust/security/compliance page exists on the site (sitemap lists only home, product, pricing, contact, privacy, terms, and use-case pages) and no SOC 2 mention appears anywhere on the marketing site or in the full docs dump (llms-full.txt). Absence of any attestation claim on a small hosted-browser SaaS with no dedicated security page is treated as not (yet) attested.

hipaa.quote: PAYG / Starter / Base / Advanced browser-hour plans; Reserved dedicated fleet from-rate.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Surfsky is a hosted antidetect/automation browser for scraping, ad verification, and agent web access; no HIPAA/BAA language appears on the marketing site, privacy policy, terms, or in the full docs dump, and the product is not positioned for regulated healthcare workloads.
